lines: Open. Four years shut and open, and I have not sat down since I did it.
No day, no list, no ceremony. You walk in through them when you have decided to.
Go home first. Everybody who has ever done well up there went home first.
Eight. Let me see them. Yes. All eight, and I have read what you did with the week after.
Stand at the counter and let me do this properly. I have been waiting four years to do it properly.
Eight, and I am not going to open anything today, and you know why.
There is a sea out there behaving in a way no Master has an answer for.
The Ascent will keep. It has kept for four years. Go and do the other thing.
Five. Let me see them. Yes. Briarbell, Stonewake, Tideglass, Emberfall, Mirehaven.
That is a real five and you got them in a real order.
Come back with eight and I will open the doors myself. Not before. Not for anyone.
Eight Crests. It is the only rule this building has and it is not mine to bend.
Look at anything out here for as long as you like.
The doors have been shut for four years. Somebody is going to open them.
I am going to stand here until somebody makes me leave. It is a very good door.
Do not rush. I have waited eighty-nine places on a list, I can wait for you.
Eighty-ninth. Eighty-ninth of three hundred and eleven and I have checked it twice.
Eighty-one names and more gaps than names, and today the gaps stopped being the sad part.
Four of those years were people who were not quite ready. This one was a year with weather in it.
I have written that in the margin. Somebody will rub it out and I will write it again.
Eighty-one Champions and more gaps than names. People find that grim.
I find it honest. It is a hard thing and it is meant to be a hard thing.
The gaps are not failures. They are years when nobody was quite ready.
The northern road opened on Thursday. Frostmere and Skyreach and I am going tonight.
Six months I have been in this room getting worse at everything.
I am going to be extremely bad at it out there instead. That is an improvement.
Six. Frostmere and Skyreach left and the northern road has been shut for eleven days.
So I am sitting in the registry looking at a wall of gold names
and getting slowly, magnificently worse at everything.
Sixty-one years and I have never heard those doors. I did not know they made a noise.
I have put my name back on the wall of failures in pencil, on the back, as usual.
Somebody will rub it off. I would like a turn at rubbing off somebody else's.
Got through two Masters, in the year sixty. Lost to the third and never went back.
No, my name is not on the wall of failures. Nobody's is. That was kind of them.
I put it on myself, in pencil, on the back. Somebody rubs it off. I put it back.
I signed it again. You are allowed to sign it twice, I asked.
I am nine and the doors are open and that is two things now.
I signed the register of intent. You are allowed. It says anyone.
I am nine. It commits you to nothing. It says so.
The one through the window has not stopped. Doors opened and she did not look up.
Same switch. Slightly better each time. Six in the morning until eleven at night.
That is what is behind those doors. Not a road. Her.
Watch the one through the window doing the same switch over and over.
That is a Master's second. Been at it since six this morning.
Everybody thinks the Summit is about the eight Crests. The Crests are the easy part.
